insight.title: Pydantic AI: make the agent boundary typed before making it bigger
insight.one_liner: Pydantic AI makes agent I/O, dependencies and tools explicit typed contracts; evals, observability and durable execution remain adjacent quality/runtime capabilities rather than properties of typing itself.
insight.why_this_matters: Typed boundaries are a practical way to reduce ambiguity in agent applications without pretending a Python framework alone provides authorization, durable state or production governance.

whole_source_map.problem: Agent applications often rely on loosely specified model outputs, tool arguments and runtime context, so interface failures appear late and are difficult to reason about.
whole_source_map.thesis: Use a typed agent object with validated outputs/tools and explicit RunContext dependencies, then compose evaluation, observability and durability around that core contract.

derived_model.problem: An agent can be functionally capable while its application boundaries remain implicit and fragile.
derived_model.mechanism: Declare output types, tool signatures and dependencies as runtime-validated contracts; add capabilities and evals around the same agent object for adjacent concerns.
derived_model.result: Application code becomes easier to type-check, test and inspect, while broader production controls remain separate responsibilities.

central_chain: The agent has an explicit typed output contract.
Tool signatures become schemas and arguments are validated before tool code runs.
RunContext carries typed runtime dependencies into tools/instructions.
Capabilities compose additional behavior without redefining the core contract.
Evals/instrumentation test and observe behavior, while durability/governance remain separate runtime concerns.
open_gaps: Typing cannot prove semantic correctness or business authorization.
The framework evolves quickly; provider/capability breadth is not the durable mental model.

nodes.label: CONTRACT
nodes.title: Typed input / output

nodes.label: CONTEXT
nodes.title: Dependencies + tools
nodes.text: RunContext supplies explicit runtime dependencies while validated tools cross the application boundary.

nodes.label: QUALITY / RUNTIME

image.reason: The important distinction is responsibility layering; a compact contract/context/runtime diagram is clearer than decorative framework imagery.

concepts.name: Typed agent contract
concepts.why_needed: Structured outputs give downstream code a validated application boundary instead of free-form model text.

concepts.name: RunContext dependency injection
concepts.why_needed: Runtime services/data can be explicit typed dependencies rather than hidden globals or ad-hoc prompt state.

concepts.name: Validated tool boundary
concepts.why_needed: Tool signatures become schemas and arguments are validated before side-effecting application code executes.

concepts.name: Agent evaluation surface
concepts.why_needed: Behavior still needs examples/evals and instrumentation after structural typing is correct.

tool_map.name: Pydantic AI Agent
tool_map.why_explore: Use one small output_type + tool example to see how output, tool schema and RunContext contracts fit together.

tool_map.name: Pydantic Evals
tool_map.why_explore: Separates behavioral testing from the typed runtime contract instead of treating type correctness as quality evidence.
tool_map.relationship: Official adjacent evaluation surface referenced by the repository.

examples.scenario: An agent must return sentiment with a bounded numeric score and may call a review lookup tool.
examples.question: Can output and tool boundaries reject structurally invalid results before application code relies on them?

examples.scenario: An agent prepares a customer update using injected service dependencies.
examples.question: Which errors are prevented by typed RunContext/tool schemas, and which authorization/side-effect controls still belong outside the SDK?

limitations: Type validation checks structure, not truth, policy compliance or semantic quality.
Validated tool arguments do not make a consequential side effect authorized or idempotent.
Pydantic Evals is an evaluation surface but is not identical to historical replay evaluation in the existing production-agent model.
Durable execution is provided through integrations/capabilities and should not be attributed to the core typed loop by default.

use_now: Define explicit output types and tool argument schemas for any agent result that downstream application code will trust.
try: Build a small Agent with output_type, one RunContext dependency and one tool, then deliberately send invalid tool/output shapes and observe where validation fails.
build: A typed extraction or decision-support agent whose runtime dependencies and outputs have no implicit dictionaries/string parsing.
watch: Which Pydantic AI capabilities remain stable as the framework expands across voice, durable execution and harness features.
ignore_for_now: Treating every Pydantic AI capability as a universal requirement for agent architecture.

connections: controlled execution: broader production governance remains outside the typed SDK boundary
ReAct: a specific reasoning/action method, not equivalent to Pydantic AI's generic agent loop
durable execution: attachable integration responsibility, not evidence that the core typed loop persists progress itself

concepts.label: Typed agent contract
concepts.summary: A runtime-validated schema boundary for agent inputs/outputs that downstream application code can rely on structurally.

concepts.label: RunContext dependency injection
concepts.summary: Passing typed runtime dependencies and context explicitly into agent instructions and tools rather than relying on hidden global state.

concepts.label: Validated tool boundary
concepts.summary: Deriving tool schemas from typed functions and validating arguments before application-side tool code executes.

concepts.label: Agent evaluation surface
concepts.summary: A dedicated test/evaluation layer for measuring agent behavior beyond structural type correctness.

relations.rationale: Typed outputs and typed runtime dependencies form complementary boundaries around one agent application run.
Tools can receive explicit typed runtime dependencies through RunContext while their call arguments are validated against function schemas.
Structural correctness is necessary but behavioral quality requires a separate evaluation/test surface.
